production.waterSource: Local groundwater is filtered and purified through the distillery's water-treatment system before use in production.
production.malt: M&H uses unpeated malted barley for standard production and runs a two-week peated production session at approximately 40 ppm every six months.
production.fermentation: Six washbacks are used with specialty dry whisky yeast. The official distillery states a fermentation duration of 60-72 hours.
production.stills: M&H uses double distillation in custom-made traditional copper pot stills. The spirit cut is relatively short, beginning around 80% ABV and ending around 70%, producing new make at approximately 75% ABV.
production.peat: Standard production is unpeated; a dedicated peated run at approximately 40 ppm is carried out periodically.
production.maturation: Whisky is matured for at least three years without climate control across several Israeli climate zones. The cask programme includes new oak, ex-bourbon and rye, STR wine casks, kosher sherry butts, rum, Cognac, Islay whisky and Israeli wine casks.

houseCharacter: M&H uses a conventional malt base and copper-pot double distillation but adapts fermentation and maturation to Israel's hot climate. A 60-72 hour fermentation and relatively narrow spirit cut create a sweet, grassy, medium-bodied new make, while the absence of climate control subjects casks to intense regional temperature and humidity differences. The resulting house character is cask-active and concentrated, with maturation location functioning as a major production variable.
cask23Narrative: M&H is built around the idea that climate itself can become part of whisky production. The spirit is made with familiar malt-whisky tools—malted barley, 60-72 hour fermentation and copper pot stills—but its casks mature across dramatically different Israeli environments, from Tel Aviv to the Dead Sea. For the customer, that makes M&H a particularly clear demonstration of how heat and humidity can reshape extraction, evaporation and maturation speed.
